_doc: Story scenes and lines. A scene is shown between chapters: a list of [speaker, text] lines, a place and who stands on stage. 'hero' = the leading player's hero (their own name is shown). Lines (banter + boss lines) are said during play in a speech strip at the top of the screen, never over the fight. choice: the last scene's two endings. speakers: who each speaker is and how they look (a foe/boss id to borrow the 3D look from, or a Chibi look).

lines: They came over the mill bridge before the cocks crowed. Rook Gang, all of them.
They didn't want our grain. They pulled the bell-stone right out of the square.
Then the road is open, and the old thing under it is restless.
The stone's just a stone, Brother. Isn't it?
Every village on the Wyrmroad keeps one. Bring it back, child. I taught you to fight for days like this.
And mind your temper. A thief can still be talked to.
Enough! You hit like a mule, I'll give you that.
You think you're the hero of this, don't you? Ask your priest who's paying for what.
He's running for Thornwood. With the stone.
The Rooks have gone to ground in the old forest. There's a witch in there who gives them shelter.
Grell said to ask you who's paying for what.
Thieves say anything when they're losing. Go. Bring the stone home.
Stop. Stop! You've made your point, little blade.
Look at the chest the Rooks left. Look at the seal on it.
A lantern. That's the Order's seal.
Someone is paying good silver for those stones. And the stones are the only thing holding it down.
Walk east, down to the docks at Saltmere. You'll see who comes for them.
You again. Fine. Since you're here, you might as well see it.
Seven bell-stones, crated under the fish. We've been stealing them before the Order can.
Lantern Guard's coming up the pier now. Pick a side, farm-hand.
You fool. The Lamplord promised you'd bring the stones to us yourself.
Ask your teacher what he calls himself at Greyspire.
She's gone off the end of the pier. Come on. If your priest is who I think he is, you'll want me with you.
You found the stones. All seven. You've done so well.
Brother, the Guard said you are the Lamplord.
I'm sorry, child. I needed someone who wouldn't ask questions until the work was done.
Take them up to the lantern. And keep my student busy.
Too late. Seven stones, seven chains, and every one of them is mine now.
When the wyrm wakes it will wake on a leash. My leash.
You'll kill everyone on the road!
Only the ones standing on it.
The road's moving. The whole road is moving!
You don't understand. It was never asleep. It was held.
The first Lamplords chained it here and built a road on its back so no one would remember.
And now Aldric wants to hold the chain himself.
...He told us it was a monster.
THE LAST CHAIN IS AT MY CROWN. COME, SMALL ONE.
One more stone and it's done. One more and it does whatever I say.
You taught me a thief can still be talked to.
I taught you what I needed you to know. Come here and I'll teach you one more thing.
Wait. Wait! If you break the chain it will be free. Do you know what a free wyrm does?
SMALL ONE. THE CHAIN IS IN YOUR HAND.

choice.prompt: The last chain is in your hand.

lines: It's... flying. The whole mountain is flying.
The bells are ringing in every village. All by themselves.
Then the road's just a road now.
A road with a lot of Rooks on it who could use honest work. Coming?
Put it down. Put the lantern down.
Someone has to hold it. Better me than him.
I WILL WAIT. I AM VERY GOOD AT WAITING.

ch1_b2: They've taken the cart road. Go!
ch2_b1: Wolves. The Rooks must feed them.
ch3_b1: Guard on the left! Don't let them near the crates!
ch3_b2: Priests. Hit the priests first or they'll patch everyone up.
ch4_b1: Zealots. They go up like lamp oil when they drop. Stand back.
ch4_b2: That thing is solid stone. Knock it off its feet with something heavy.
ch6_b1: Turn back, child. This is not your road.
grell_start: Back for more? You can't have it.
